neighbours.label: the token after an offering 'Here' when handing something over in speech (Here, take this / Here you go)
fire: She pulled a scarf from her bag. "Here, put this on before you freeze."
The nurse smiled and said, "Here you are, two tablets with water."
He tossed me the keys. "Here, you drive for a while."
My sister came in and said, "Here, hold the baby while I find the bottle."
My grandmother handed me a plate. "Here, eat something before you go."
The clerk slid the form across the counter and said, "Here you go, sign at the bottom."
Seeing him shiver, she held out her coat. "Here, take mine."
The vendor wrapped the bread and said, "Here ya go, still warm."

My sister came in and said, "Hold the baby while I find the bottle."

Seeing him shiver, she closed the window. "It's cold in here."
The vendor wrapped the bread and said, "That will be three euros."
